variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
(local x 10)
(var y 20)
(set y 30)

;; let binds local variables for a scope
(let [a 1
      b 2]
  (+ a b))

;; Global variable
(global z 100)
variables.notes: local creates immutable local variables, var creates mutable locals, and set changes a var. let creates block-scoped locals.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
42                   ; number
3.14                 ; number
"Hello"              ; string
true                 ; boolean true
false                ; boolean false
nil                  ; nil
[1 2 3]              ; sequential table (array)
{:a 1 :b 2}          ; associative table (map)
:symbol              ; string (compiles to Lua string)
data_types.notes: Fennel types directly map to Lua types. There's only one numeric type. Tables serve as both arrays and dictionaries.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
(+ 1 2)      ; => 3
(- 10 4)     ; => 6
(* 2 3)      ; => 6
(/ 10 2)     ; => 5
(// 10 3)    ; => 3 (integer division)
(% 10 3)     ; => 1 (modulo)
(.. "a" "b") ; => "ab" (string concat)

(= 1 1)      ; equality
(not= 1 2)   ; inequality
(and true false)
(or false true)
(not true)
operators.notes: Operators are prefix just like in other Lisps, but map directly to Lua's math and logic operators. .. is used for string concatenation.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
(if (> x 0)
    "positive"
    "negative")

(if (> x 0) "positive"
    (< x 0) "negative"
    "zero") ; multi-way if

(when (> x 0)
  (print "positive"))
conditionals.notes: if acts like an expression and can have an arbitrary number of condition/result pairs. when evaluates a body only if the condition is truthy.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
;; Numeric for loop
(for [i 1 10]
  (print i))

(for [i 10 1 -1] ; With step
  (print i))

;; Iterating over sequential tables
(each [index value (ipairs ["a" "b" "c"])]
  (print index value))
for_loop.notes: for implements Lua's numeric for loop. each implements Lua's generic for loop using iterators like ipairs and pairs.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: while directly compiles to Lua's while loop. It evaluates its body repeatedly as long as the condition is truthy.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
(fn add [a b]
  (+ a b))

;; Anonymous function (lambda)
(lambda [x] (* x x))
;; or
(hashfn (* $1 $1)) ; or #(* $1 $1)

;; Variadic function
(fn sum [...]
  (let [args [...]]
    ;; logic to sum args
    ))
functions.notes: fn defines functions. lambda or λ define functions that perform arity checks. hashfn provides a short syntax for simple anonymous functions.

arrays.title: Arrays (Sequential Tables)
arrays.code:
(local arr [10 20 30])

;; Accessing (1-indexed)
(. arr 1) ; => 10

;; Modifying
(tset arr 1 42)

;; Appending
(table.insert arr 40)

;; Length
(length arr)
arrays.notes: Arrays in Fennel are Lua sequential tables. They use square brackets and are 1-indexed. The . macro gets values, tset sets values.

maps.title: Maps (Associative Tables)
maps.code:
(local t {:key "value"
          :number 42})

;; Accessing
(. t :key) ; => "value"
t.key      ; Syntax sugar for (. t :key)

;; Modifying
(tset t :key "new-value")

;; Iterating
(each [k v (pairs t)]
  (print k v))
maps.notes: Maps are Lua associative tables using curly braces. String keys can be written as keywords (e.g., :key). . and tset are used for access and modification.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
;; Using pcall (protected call) like Lua
(local (ok? result) (pcall (fn [] (error "fail"))))
(if ok?
    (print "Success: " result)
    (print "Error: " result))

;; Throwing an error
(error "Something went wrong")
error_handling.notes: Error handling uses Lua's pcall or xpcall to catch errors, returning a boolean indicating success and either the result or the error message.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
;; Single-line comment in Lisp
#|
 Multi-line block comment
|#
(defun add (a b)
  "Documentation string for function"
  (+ a b))
comments.notes: Fennel uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
(def x 42)          ; Integer
(def pi 3.14159)    ; Float
(def ratio 1/3)     ; Exact rational ratio
(def hex #xFF)      ; Hexadecimal
numbers.notes: Fennel supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Fennel treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Fennel performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.code:
(def s "Hello, World!")
(def char-val (char s 0))
(def multi "Line 1
Line 2")
strings.notes: Fennel represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Fennel formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Fennel, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Fennel constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.notes: Fennel achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Fennel emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Fennel are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Fennel uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Fennel provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Fennel isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
